question.text: Vikram buys a stock at INR 200, receives a dividend of INR 8, and sells it at INR 230 after one year. What is the Holding Period Return (HPR)?

explanation.text: The Logic: Per NISM Series X-A page 271, yearly return is the portfolio price gain or loss plus dividends or other cash distributions expressed as a percent of invested assets. HPR = (Income + End Value - Begin Value) / Begin Value = (8 + 230 - 200) / 200 = 38/200 = 19.00%. The HPR captures both capital gain (15%) and dividend yield (4%). The Trap: 15.00% considers only the capital gain (30/200) and ignores the dividend. 18.00% adds the dividend to the selling price but divides by 210 (average of buy and sell). 16.52% divides the total gain by the ending value (38/230). Note: Always include cash distributions (dividends, interest) in the numerator and divide by the initial invested amount.
